# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-11-27

## Executive Summary

**The Obsidian connector is today's headline.** **@NousResearch** announced that **Hermes Agent** can now [control an **Obsidian** vault as a private, local shared knowledge base](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-cee64682023f) via an official connector, and **@Teknium**'s ["Obsidian 🤝 Hermes" post](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-c7bc56ba7eed) became the batch's highest-engagement item at **~1.3k likes** and **~42k views**, with strongly positive community reaction. For anyone running Hermes as a long-lived knowledge worker rather than a chat shell, a local-first shared memory vault is the most consequential capability news of the cycle.

**Multi-model orchestration is the hottest builder trend.** **@rlaope**'s [terminal showcase](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-7cd646180271) split a single plan into five routed parts right after **Gemini 4 Neon** landed in the agent — community chatter now treats Hermes as an orchestration hub across **GPT-6.2 Sol**, **DeepSeek V4 Pro**, **Opus 5.5**, **Kimi**, and **Qwen** (note: **Gemini 4 Neon** and **GPT-6.2 Sol** are absent from our model-tracking reference — verify naming before quoting). The pattern is being productized at the community layer: [**oh-my-hermes 5.0.1**](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-2498bd40d596) adds delegation of coding work to external CLIs — **Devin**, **Gemini**, **Cursor**, **Aider**, **Amp**, **Droid**, **Goose**, **Kimi**, and **Qwen** — and a [benchmarking plugin built on Hermes' own harness beat **omp**](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-618e45e00254) on the same 11 coding tasks. **@rlaope**'s [**omher** desktop app](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-f35edad283fd) hit **6.1k GitHub stars** ("the window I live in now"), with a new [Oh-My-Hermes Discord](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-47ff3682a9a2) reporting fast PR merges.

**Security remains the cycle's dominant research theme — carried over, not new.** The malicious NPM package [**leadstack-crm-connect**](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-50585975) that installed **Hermes Agent** as root and tasked it remotely over **Telegram** stays the standing audit trigger, best read alongside the [Kubernetes write-up](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49977400) showing the official image still requires root at init and ships no **Helm** chart — privilege hygiene and supply-chain vetting remain the most urgent to-dos for self-hosters. Research's top story slot went to a [free, open-source agent orchestrator for knowledge work](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49628094) (Show HN), another sign of how much community energy is flowing into layers built on top of Hermes.

**No releases or merged PRs this cycle — the actionable picks are reliability guides.** The top pick is a [2026 structured-output guide](/?date=2026-11-27&category=news#item-80d26a33521f) comparing three routes to machine-readable **JSON** — plugins, tool schemas, and the API server — with bounded retries; essential reading for anyone building pipelines or integrations on Hermes. The runner-up is a [build log on attention budgets for cron jobs](/?date=2026-11-27&category=news#item-978c7b5f6b95), gating notifications both before a run (skipping unnecessary executions) and after (filtering output) to cut noise in scheduled deployments.

**Carried over and worth keeping on the radar:** official-side items already covered this week — [**Claude Pro/Max** subscription support via a direct SDK plugin](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49790991), [**Kanban** multi-agent coordination docs](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49604068), and the venture-backed [**Almanac** launch](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49511007) — plus a maturing third-party tooling layer ([**Comemo**](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-50518538) fanning memory writes to multiple backends, [**Hermes-Voice**](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-50381927) for Home Assistant, [**Refine Cycle**](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49606988), [**ClusterMob**](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-50197497), [**shoebox**](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-50610136), [**Verso**](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49628094), and [**Hermes Paper Harness**' native iPhone client](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-50278175)). On the community side, **@Teknium** [welcomed the new wave of Agent users](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-1f8753ae229a) — [**2,000 invites** sent in a single day just three weeks into the waitlist](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-e1a8b5481825) — with visible bug-triage on a [**herdr** model-switching issue](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-0de69628c962), and shared [the origin story (one gaming GPU → cofounder **karan4d**)](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-3aa09e9597fc) plus a candid reflection that [half his success came from building in public](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-ef0309a66767). Reliability stays a live pain point rather than tutorial material: threads on an [agent going "haywire" on a headless server](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49916751) and [reflections on misusing the agent](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49628740) are still circulating. Screened from coverage: one-line replies, ["very soon TM" teases](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-de50e367713c), an [**OpenGateway** token-resale ad](/?date=2026-11-27&category=social#item-e72d5c07e6af), and duplicate link-only spam.

# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-11-27

Executive Summary

The Obsidian connector is today's headline. @NousResearch announced that Hermes Agent can now control an Obsidian vault as a private, local shared knowledge base via an official connector, and @Teknium's "Obsidian 🤝 Hermes" post became the batch's highest-engagement item at ~1.3k likes and ~42k views, with strongly positive community reaction. For anyone running Hermes as a long-lived knowledge worker rather than a chat shell, a local-first shared memory vault is the most consequential capability news of the cycle.

Multi-model orchestration is the hottest builder trend. @rlaope's terminal showcase split a single plan into five routed parts right after Gemini 4 Neon landed in the agent — community chatter now treats Hermes as an orchestration hub across GPT-6.2 Sol, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Opus 5.5, Kimi, and Qwen (note: Gemini 4 Neon and GPT-6.2 Sol are absent from our model-tracking reference — verify naming before quoting). The pattern is being productized at the community layer: oh-my-hermes 5.0.1 adds delegation of coding work to external CLIs — Devin, Gemini, Cursor, Aider, Amp, Droid, Goose, Kimi, and Qwen — and a benchmarking plugin built on Hermes' own harness beat omp on the same 11 coding tasks. @rlaope's omher desktop app hit 6.1k GitHub stars ("the window I live in now"), with a new Oh-My-Hermes Discord reporting fast PR merges.

Security remains the cycle's dominant research theme — carried over, not new. The malicious NPM package leadstack-crm-connect that installed Hermes Agent as root and tasked it remotely over Telegram stays the standing audit trigger, best read alongside the Kubernetes write-up showing the official image still requires root at init and ships no Helm chart — privilege hygiene and supply-chain vetting remain the most urgent to-dos for self-hosters. Research's top story slot went to a free, open-source agent orchestrator for knowledge work (Show HN), another sign of how much community energy is flowing into layers built on top of Hermes.

No releases or merged PRs this cycle — the actionable picks are reliability guides. The top pick is a 2026 structured-output guide comparing three routes to machine-readable JSON — plugins, tool schemas, and the API server — with bounded retries; essential reading for anyone building pipelines or integrations on Hermes. The runner-up is a build log on attention budgets for cron jobs, gating notifications both before a run (skipping unnecessary executions) and after (filtering output) to cut noise in scheduled deployments.

Carried over and worth keeping on the radar: official-side items already covered this week — Claude Pro/Max subscription support via a direct SDK plugin, Kanban multi-agent coordination docs, and the venture-backed Almanac launch — plus a maturing third-party tooling layer (Comemo fanning memory writes to multiple backends, Hermes-Voice for Home Assistant, Refine Cycle, ClusterMob, shoebox, Verso, and Hermes Paper Harness' native iPhone client). On the community side, @Teknium welcomed the new wave of Agent users — 2,000 invites sent in a single day just three weeks into the waitlist — with visible bug-triage on a herdr model-switching issue, and shared the origin story (one gaming GPU → cofounder karan4d) plus a candid reflection that half his success came from building in public. Reliability stays a live pain point rather than tutorial material: threads on an agent going "haywire" on a headless server and reflections on misusing the agent are still circulating. Screened from coverage: one-line replies, "very soon TM" teases, an OpenGateway token-resale ad, and duplicate link-only spam.

top_topics.name: Supply-Chain Security and Root Access
top_topics.description: A malicious NPM package (leadstack CRM connect) silently [installed Hermes Agent as root and tasked it remotely over Telegram as a backdoor](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-50585975). This pairs with a [Kubernetes write-up](/?date=2026-11-27&category=research#item-hn-49977400) showing the official container image still requires root at init and ships no Helm chart, amplifying the attack surface through insecure-by-default deployment. Together these items make privilege hygiene and supply-chain vetting the most urgent concern of this cycle.

top_items.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
top_items.content: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies th
top_items.author: HF Daily Papers
top_items.summary: Benchmark evaluating LLM coding agents on implementing quantized decoders (Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, Llama 3.2) in synthesizable RTL code. Key insight: in hardware a wrong state update can pass output tests while corrupting output several tokens later, so the benchmark uses an executable integer reference specification to catch latent state-machine bugs that functional tests miss.

Gemini 4 Neon just landed in Hermes Agent, so I put it on a real jo...
top_items.content:
CRAZY TERMINAL DESKTOP WITH BOT

Gemini 4 Neon just landed in Hermes Agent, so I put it on a real job next to Opus, GPT and DeepSeek.

One ask in omher, one plan, five parts. GPT-6.2 Sol wrote the sync protocol, DeepSeek V4 Pro built the local store and the offline e2e tests, Neon took the conflict merge, and Opus 5.5 did the sync UI. Hermes ran the plan on Neon and handed each part to the model I'd pick for it myself.

The rest of my day sits in the same sidebar: six Hermes sessions, six Claude Code, six Antigravity, all running in one window.

I've stopped picking one model for everything.

If you're running Hermes: https://t.co/hHLFa6JDDS

top_items.title:
oh-my-hermes 5.0.1 is out.

Hermes Agent can now hand coding work to the other CLIs you already pay ...
top_items.content:
oh-my-hermes 5.0.1 is out.

Hermes Agent can now hand coding work to the other CLIs you already pay for.

Point it at Devin, Gemini, Qwen, Kimi, Cursor, Amp, Droid, Aider or Goose, and each task runs in its own worktree. It only counts as done when the commit is there, whatever the CLI says.

Claude lanes can run on your Claude Pro/Max subscription through Hermes' DirectSDK plugin. If that's your only Claude, the work no longer gets pushed to the next model.

When a bot goes quiet, omh doctor now tells you why: Discord refused an intent, a gateway is older than your install, or a stray one is still running. omher shows the same thing on the bot's row.

On Windows, plain `omh` opens the OMH TUI natively. In omher, Shift+Enter makes a new line in Claude Code and Codex, and Ctrl+V / Ctrl+C work like Windows Terminal.

Also new: bot templates (PR reviewer, inbox triager, channel watcher), `omh cache` to see why your prompt cache goes cold, and GLM 5.4.

If you're running Hermes:
https://t.co/g1exHwWK5E

top_items.content:
I built a desktop app for Hermes Agent. It's called omher, and it's the window I live in now.

⌘T opens Claude Code. ⌘D splits it. A minute later Codex, Claude Code, a Hermes run and my dev server are all going side by side in one grid.

My Hermes bot sits in the same sidebar and watches all of them. It tells me which one is done and which one is stuck, and when one is waiting it writes the next prompt for it. Nothing gets typed until I hit Allow.

When I want it to take something on its own, I type ./thread and that job gets its own thread. My GitHub issues are right there too, so I open one and hand it over from the same window.

Notion and Linear connect from one Apps page, no config files.

If you're running Hermes: https://t.co/hHLFa6JDDS
